title: The Seventh Day
logline: On the seventh day after a death, a family cooks through the night, invites monks at dawn, and pours water until it overflows, saying a name out loud one more time.
human_question: What can the living still do for someone who is gone?

premise.story: A family's almsgiving in memory of the dead (mataka danaya), followed from the first errands to the quiet after the guests leave.
premise.place: A family home and its neighbourhood temple in a North Central province village.
premise.experience: A house rearranged for guests, a whole night's cooking, monks arriving at dawn, and the specific small ceremony of pouring water into a bowl until it overflows while a name is spoken.

concept_links.why: The source treats sharing merit with the dead as real work: simply saying 'share in this' is not enough, the deed has to be told well enough that the person who died can feel glad about it [C059-P:L239-L245]. The film can follow that telling as it actually happens in a family's kitchen and front room.

One class of unhappy being described in the source lives only on what relatives give in its name and waits for them to give it [C051-M:L21]. This is the everyday ritual behind that description, without the film asserting where the dead person now is.

what_camera_could_observe: Shopping and borrowing pots the evening before
Water poured slowly until it overflows while the family says the name
The quiet afterwards when the guests have gone
what_must_be_real: A family's own loss and their own reasons for holding the almsgiving. No line is scripted; the dedication is whatever the family actually says.

possible_arc.opening: A house being swept and rearranged before dawn.
possible_arc.turn: The meal is offered; the family's attention narrows to the moment of pouring water.
possible_arc.ending_open: The last guest leaves. What the house feels like afterward is not explained.

position_hint: opening candidate: an heirloom used in the ritual, such as a jug, a set of dishes or a framed photograph, could plausibly be where Object 8 is acquired, if the family is willing; the film also works as a strong early piece for the group on its own

requirements: A family in the days following a bereavement who wants an almsgiving filmed
A neighbourhood temple with monks able to attend
Full, ongoing consent from every family member present

suggestions.name: A village in the Anuradhapura district
suggestions.why: A common setting for this practice with a nearby village temple; suggested for texture, not for a specific household.

risks: Implying the deceased has become a suffering being
Treating a private rite as performance
drop_if: No family gives full, ongoing consent
The family does not want the ritual explained or framed on camera

connections.note: A second real moment where Object 8 could be acquired, here through ritual rather than sorting a room.
Both are about care extended toward beings ordinary comfort cannot reach directly.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
